invariant: Maximum 500 LOC per source file; decompose when nearing 450
rationale: Bounds per-file complexity and keeps files reviewable and agent-sized

invariant: `unwrap()` and `expect()` are forbidden in all Rust sources
rationale: Typed, recoverable errors at boundaries; panics are never an acceptable failure mode
sensor: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings (unwrap_used/expect_used deny) + python3 scripts/validate-structure.py

invariant: No unsafe code in the workspace
rationale: Eliminates undefined-behavior classes from the privacy boundary

invariant: Runtime crates stay provider-agnostic: no cloud LLM SDK or network-client dependency
rationale: The privacy boundary must work offline and never leak context to a provider
sensor: bash scripts/check-deps.sh + cargo deny check (crates.io-only allow-list) + review of new dependency entries

invariant: Every detector, judge, policy, transformer, and vault implementation stays replaceable behind plugin-api traits
rationale: Capabilities must remain swappable and testable in isolation
sensor: cargo check --workspace (implementations compile against plugin-api) + review of new capability crates

invariant: Registry names map to the intended plugins and unknown names fail with a capability-naming error; `hybrid` wires regex together with the model half, so it fails closed without a model_dir instead of degrading to regex
rationale: The names are the user-facing selection surface for CLI and MCP; a silently remapped or degraded name would change what detects and transforms without any other sensor noticing

invariant: Secrets are redacted, never pseudonymized; personal identifiers are pseudonymized
rationale: A reversible token for a secret would defeat the redaction guarantee

invariant: Raw sensitive input, vault mappings, and restored secrets are never logged or echoed outside the sanitized/blob contract
rationale: Logs and error messages are context that can leave the machine
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-core --test privacy_invariants && cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server (raw-value egress assertions)

invariant: Stage error text is scrubbed of the values the pipeline has seen (input plus detected entity values) before it leaves, so a plugin that formats raw input or an original value into its error cannot leak it to stderr, an MCP response, or a log
rationale: Plugins are replaceable and their error strings are arbitrary; the pipeline, not the backend, owns the guarantee that raw values never cross the boundary

invariant: Mappings are scoped by an explicit session id; restore resolves only tokens of the same scope and vault
rationale: Prevents cross-task placeholder resolution and leaks between concurrent agents
sensor: cargo test --workspace (scope-isolation tests in privacy-core, plugin-process, mcp-server)

invariant: Process plugins fail closed: malformed response, invalid span, undecided entity, leftover value, unresolvable placeholder, or non-zero exit stops the call instead of passing text through
rationale: A permissive plugin turns the privacy boundary into a passthrough

invariant: MCP stdio tools/list stays in fixed order with ttlMs/cacheScope metadata, and the server/discover and initialize paths resolve to identical tool behavior
rationale: Clients cache tool lists; order and metadata drift breaks that contract silently

invariant: GLiNER2 stays behind the opt-in gliner2 feature, requires a local model directory, and fails closed without one
rationale: Heavy ONNX dependencies must not burden the default build, and models are never fetched automatically
sensor: cargo check -p do-context-shield-detector-gliner2 --features gliner2 (feature build; not part of the default suite)

invariant: Conventional commits with a type prefix; PR titles stay conventional because squash merges reuse them as the commit subject
rationale: Machine-parseable history for release drafting and commitlint

invariant: Agent skills pass the structure gate and carry graded eval fixtures
rationale: Skills are load-bearing feedforward guides; unvalidated guidance drifts silently

invariant: A change is complete only when verification evidence for its signal set is green
rationale: Exit codes and recorded evidence, not self-assessment, prove completion
sensor: do-harness verify --set verification --record + do-harness status --set verification

invariant: A sensor failing 3 consecutive times on the same subtask halts the loop and records its error signature
rationale: Blind re-runs of a broken sensor waste the loop and hide the defect
sensor: do-harness verify --record (strike counters) + do-harness errors list

invariant: Hooks come from .githooks via core.hooksPath; do-harness hook install into .git/hooks is the per-developer alternative, never both at once
rationale: A core.hooksPath pointing at .githooks makes git ignore .git/hooks entirely
sensor: review + do-harness doctor (reports managed-hook presence and state-db skew)

invariant: Semantic judges classify existing candidates only: they return labels and confidence, never spans or text, and a judge can never downgrade a secret-like kind from redaction
rationale: A judge that could invent spans or rewrite values would move the privacy boundary into a model

invariant: A judge failure, an out-of-range or duplicated judgment index, or an out-of-range confidence fails the sanitize call closed
rationale: A judge trusted without validation turns a malformed response into a silent policy bypass

invariant: Recipient-aware default policy enforces GDPR/jurisdiction data categories: special-category data addressed to external or unknown recipients blocks, and unknown recipients block non-secret data except when it is explicitly declared non-personal
rationale: Fail-closed boundary prevents sensitive personal data from leaking to unvetted recipients

invariant: Detector output is validated centrally for a non-empty kind, confidence in 0..=1, UTF-8 character boundaries, input bounds, value matching, and non-overlapping spans before judging or planning
rationale: Downstream pipeline stages (judge, policy, transformer) must never encounter corrupted offsets or overlapping entity replacements, and an empty kind or NaN/out-of-range confidence from an in-process detector must fail the call closed instead of reaching policy decisions or results

invariant: Vault lifecycle supports explicit session deletion and TTL expiration; JSON vault serializes concurrent writers via file locking
rationale: Session cleanup bounds storage and protects privacy after agent tasks conclude; file locking prevents race conditions in multi-process workflows

invariant: JSON vault persistence surfaces every write failure before renaming, so a failed flush can never replace a healthy vault file or report success; a vault file deleted outside the process reloads as empty instead of resurrecting stale mappings
rationale: A BufWriter discards flush errors when it drops, which silently corrupted the vault on ENOSPC/I/O failure while the insert reported success; and honoring an external deletion is what keeps the on-disk file the source of truth for sequential processes

invariant: MCP tools reside in the context.* namespace and context.restore strictly requires an explicit session
rationale: Restoration resolves raw values and must never default to a shared or implicit session scope

invariant: The MCP surface defaults to the model-safe tool set: `mcp-stdio` exposes only `context.sanitize` and `context.inspect` unless `--tools` opts into `restore`/`forget`/`all`, because MCP tool results return to the calling model and a model-driven restore hands raw values into the context the boundary protects
rationale: Restore resolves raw values and forget destroys mappings; exposing them to a prompt-injected model lets it un-sanitize text it holds or destroy the harness's ability to restore. The fail-closed default keeps the model-facing surface non-revealing, and the CLI remains the harness-side restore path.
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server + cargo test -p do-context-shield (tests/mcp_stdio.rs, tests/cli_errors.rs)

invariant: Adapter context surfaces default to the most restrictive ProcessingContext and reject unknown recipient/data_category names or wrong argument types instead of silently downgrading
rationale: A typo in a client-supplied trust classification must fail the call, never weaken the recipient-aware policy
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server + CLI value parsers (clap value_parser + sanitize smoke)

invariant: Adapter argument surfaces are enforced, not just declared: CLI sanitize/restore/forget require an explicit --session, and MCP tools/call rejects a non-object `arguments` or a missing/non-string `text` instead of silently operating on empty input
rationale: An implicit session scope lets concurrent tasks resolve each other's placeholders, and a silent empty-input success hides a malformed client call behind a plausible response
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield (tests/cli_errors.rs session_is_required_exits_2) + cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server (missing_or_non_string_text_is_rejected, non_object_arguments_is_rejected)

invariant: Session mappings are deletable through explicit forget surfaces (MCP context.forget, CLI forget) that require a session, and a process vault must confirm deletion with deleted=true or the call fails closed
rationale: Retention must be bounded and a child that silently ignores a wipe would leave raw values resolvable

invariant: The configuration file may only select known plugins and context names; unknown fields or values fail startup, and a CLI flag outranks the file, which outranks the built-in default
rationale: A config typo must never silently select a weaker plugin, and effective settings must not depend on which clap default happened to be compiled in
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield (config module tests: unknown field/value rejected, CLI-over-config precedence)

invariant: CLI and MCP stdio behavior is tested black-box against the compiled `do-context-shield` binary, spawned with a hermetic working directory and `$HOME` so ambient config files can never change a test outcome
rationale: Behavior in the shipped artifact, not library internals, is the contract; a test reading the developer's real HOME or cwd config would be non-reproducible

invariant: Detector overlap dedup keeps the longest span and resolves equal-span ties by SPECS order: more specific kinds precede looser shapes, and semantic post-filters (Luhn for card numbers, ABA for US routing numbers) run before dedup
rationale: A looser pattern can match exactly the same text as a more specific kind, so list order decides the reported kind; filtering invalid candidates after dedup would silently drop the specific match

invariant: CodeQL code scanning runs through GitHub default setup (rust, python, actions) and must stay configured, because the main branch ruleset requires code-scanning results before a pull request can merge
rationale: With default setup disabled, or with no analysis on the target branch, the ruleset's code_scanning rule can never be satisfied and every merge needs an administrator bypass; an advanced-setup workflow added alongside default setup fails at analysis upload instead of taking over
sensor: gh api repos/d-oit/do-context-shield/code-scanning/default-setup (state=configured) + gh api repos/d-oit/do-context-shield/rulesets/rule-suites (code_scanning rule result)

invariant: Hybrid detector merge keeps primary spans authoritative and resolves secondary-secondary overlaps longest-span-wins, keeping the earlier-returned span on equal lengths
rationale: The merged list must carry no overlapping secondary spans so hybrid output is stable before the pipeline's own dedup pass, while primary precedence stops a noisy model fragment from splitting an authoritative structured-identifier span

invariant: The GLiNER2 backend loads ONNX Runtime dynamically and needs a runtime matching the ort release it was built against (1.28.x for ort 2.0.0-rc.13, supplied via ORT_DYLIB_PATH or the loader path)
rationale: ort is built with load-dynamic, so a missing or mismatched runtime fails at engine load; the version pin plus the official archive command is what users need to bring the model backend up
sensor: docs/plugins.md runtime note + gated model-backed E2E (cargo test -p do-context-shield --features gliner2 --test cli_model_e2e; skips without ORT_DYLIB_PATH + DO_CONTEXT_SHIELD_E2E_MODEL_DIR; verified 2026-09-20 with ORT 1.28.0 + fp16 fragment export)

invariant: CI runs the workspace tests on Linux with --all-features and on macOS and Windows with default features plus `cargo check --workspace --all-features --all-targets`, so platform-specific breakage in both default and feature-gated code is caught before merge
rationale: The CLI and MCP server ship as cross-platform binaries; Linux-only CI silently missed a Windows TOML path-escaping defect the first matrix run surfaced, and the native feature-gated path (gliner2/ort/tokenizers) previously only ever compiled on Linux, so a Windows/macOS build break could only surface after merge
sensor: GitHub CI: the `test` job (Linux, --all-features) and the `cross-platform` matrix (macos-latest, windows-latest: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast then cargo check --workspace --all-features --all-targets)

invariant: The shell surfaces (`scripts/*.sh`, `.githooks/*`) pass shellcheck; the sensor WARN-skips without the tool locally and fails closed in CI
rationale: The hooks and helper scripts are load-bearing contributor and CI gates; the SC2059-class printf defects a manual sweep had to fix should surface automatically instead
sensor: bash scripts/check-shellcheck.sh (shellcheck sensor, in the verification and ci sets)
